posts.text:
Most people will never achieve their goals.

They’ll sit in their comfort zones.

Then wonder why life feels empty.

Your dream client isn’t looking for perfect.

They’re looking for someone who gets shit done.

“Why is this taking so long?”

Because good work isn’t rushed.

You aren’t “bad at business”.

You’re bad at patience.

This isn’t a sprint.

It’s a fucking marathon.

Quit blaming “the algorithm”.

Your content isn’t engaging enough. Yet.

Every time you complain about “not enough clients,” ask yourself:

Have I made any effort to talk to new people this week?

DMs.

Emails.

Commenting with intention.

This is the work that builds trust.

If you’re too scared to start a conversation, the only person ghosting your 
dreams is you.

Most people stop when it gets tough.

That’s where you double down.

Every rejection means you’re closer to the ones who will say yes.

Hard doesn’t mean impossible.

It means worth it.

Clients don’t care about how many hours you work.

They care about how much value you bring.

Focus on impact over effort.

And you’ll have clients begging to work with you.

Your “follower count” doesn’t pay your bills.

Your ability to connect with the right people does.

Stop chasing clout.

Start chasing real relationships.

You’re not a failure.

Not because you’ve “tried everything.”

But because you’ve barely tried enough.

Every “failure” is a fucking lesson if you let it be.

You’re learning what doesn’t work.

What to avoid.

How to improve.

The people who win aren’t the most talented.

They’re the ones who keep fucking showing up.

So ask yourself:

Are you done yet?

Or is this just the part where you decide to keep going?

You can’t make people value your work.

But you can decide to value yourself.

Stop offering discounts out of fear.

The right clients pay without hesitation.

The wrong ones will ask for “exposure” in return.

One bad call doesn’t make you a bad designer.

One mistake doesn’t make you unprofessional.

No client is “the last chance” for your success.

You’re the one in control.

Tough conversations build trust.

Stop avoiding them.

Respect yourself enough to charge what you’re worth.

The clients who don’t like it aren’t your clients.

Your competition isn’t better than you.

They’re just louder.

You don’t need to yell to be heard.

But you do need to show up every day.

Stop trying to be perfect.

Start trying to be consistent.

Perfection gets you stuck.

Consistency gets you progress.

You’ll get ghosted.

You’ll make offers that get ignored.

You’ll have days where nothing clicks.

And then you’ll get one “yes”.

That’s all it takes to change everything.

“Starting is hard”.

So is staying broke.

So is staying invisible.

Pick your hard.

90% of websites are useless.

Not because of design.

Not because of colors.

Because they don’t speak to the customer.

Your site isn’t about you.

It’s about solving their problems.

Make your headlines scream their pain.

Make your copy tell them how life gets better when they hire you.

Stop hiding behind aesthetics.

Results win.

Your website isn’t an art piece.

It’s a tool.

To sell.

To persuade.

To convert.

Build it to work.

Most freelancers struggle because they don’t act like a business.

Track your time.

Set boundaries.

Be professional.

Even if you’re working in your pajamas.

“What if my work isn’t good enough?”

Your work isn’t supposed to be good at first.

But the market will teach you.

Every mistake is another step toward mastery.

Overthinking kills more dreams than failure ever will.

Start before you’re ready.

The most underrated skill in web design:

Listening.

Clients will tell you what they want.

Building a successful web design business is simple.

Learn the basics of design.

Learn how to market yourself.

Get your first clients.

Get better by working with real clients.

It’s not easy.

But it’s always simple.

You think you need to be "creative".

You don’t.

You need to be clear.

Your clients need clarity more than they need creativity.

You don’t get paid for the hours you put in.

You get paid for the value you deliver.

Focus on impact, not effort.

"Nobody notices my work."

That’s because you’re playing small.

Start putting your work out there.

Nobody will come looking for you.

Designing websites isn’t just about the pixels.

It’s about solving problems.

It’s about making someone’s life easier.

If your site isn’t useful, it doesn’t matter how pretty it is.

The real flex isn’t working 80 hours a week.

It’s working 20 hours a week.

And earning more than most people do in 40.

Web design will teach you three things.

How to communicate clearly.

How to sell your ideas.

How to work under pressure.

These skills will change your life if you let them.

Stop trying to make everyone like your work.

Not everyone is your client.

Not everyone needs your style.

Find the ones who do.

If you don’t know where to start, focus on one thing.

Get your first client.

That’s it.

Everything else will come later.

Freelancing isn’t about freedom.

It’s about responsibility.

The more you own that, the more freedom you get.

Every time you hesitate to post your work, someone else is posting theirs.

Their work isn’t better.

They’re just braver.

Your first website will suck.

Your first client call will be awkward.

Your first pitch will be messy.

But your tenth?

That’s where the magic starts.

Idk why nobody talks about this,

but freestyling might be the best sales skill on the entire earth.

No joke.

Tonights email is about how freestyling your way through objections might make you rich,

and also why I am scared of people actually doing it.

posts.text:
I just realized how fucked up it is that people go their entire lives without ever doing something completely insane.

Like something that makes no sense to anyone but you.

People just wake up.

Eat cereal.

Work their little job.

Come home.

Sleep.

Repeat.

And then they fucking die.

Like bro.

Jump into a lake at midnight.

Build a business that everyone says is stupid.

Run 10 miles barefoot.

Say something wild to a stranger.

Start posting online and embarrass yourself.

Do something weird.
A business is just discipline with an invoice attached.

Why I only build websites for people who already sell

I don't build websites for people who have never sold their offer once,

or people who never made a cent and then want a portfolio page.

It will just make you feel productive and waste your money.

And also you avoid the number one thing you should do in that situation.

Which is SELLING YOUR SERVICE.

Simply getting someone to say yes to what you have to offer.

Because that is the ONLY thing that matters in the beginning.

So now I only work with people who already sell stuff.

Because they have proof that their offer works, they have money to reinvest, and they actually use the website.

And they care about results

So if you haven't made a single sale yet,

go knock on doors or sell cold DMs.

But DO NOT get a website.

It's useless for you at that time.

One of the most underrated web design principles:

Information Scent.

Literally NOBODY talks about it.

But it decides if someone does something on your website or leaves instantly.

Here's how it works.

Most people don't go on websites for fun.

They go on them because they need something FAST.

And when people are in a rush, they scan instead of reading carefully.

And what they are looking for is a "scent" of what they care about aka something familiar.

Something where they get the feeling that this will solve my problem type shit.

And that is where copy comes into play.

If the scent of what they read is weak, they leave the website, but if it is strong, they stay.

And so you need to make the scent as strong as possible by improving the copywriting.

Saying shit like "Empowering your vision with digital solutions" has NO scent.

But if you say "I help gym owners get more leads through paid ads" has a certain scent.

You see what I mean?

The visitor knows what it is about immediately.

and also who it is for.

So that is exactly what you need to do.

Making the scent stronger.

Do you ever feel your excitement disappear the moment you tell someone about a win you had?

There’s a reason for that.

Tonights email is about how emotions are like scents in a closed room,

and the longer you keep the door shut, the longer the good shit stays.

posts.text:
I just realized something random as fuck while making chicken.

Every time I try to be perfect with my routine, I fuck it up.

But when I am loose and just focused on doing the work, I win.

Why did I think that waking up at 7, journaling for 30 min, meditating and visualizing would make me rich?

It just made me tired and bored.

All I needed was to drink water, get to work, and train.

That’s it.

That is ALL that I needed to change.

Work on the shit that matters.

And do it every day.

In business but also in life.
Your work is only hard when you keep thinking about it instead of just doing it.

How I Trick My Brain Into Working

This is gonna sound dumb,

But I treat myself like a fucking dog.

You know how dogs do tricks for food?

Yeah I basically do the same.

But with work.

I tell myself “Alright bro, one task and then we get a coffee”.

Boom.

Task done.

Then “Do this client revision and then we go eat breakfast”.

Boom.

Done.

You get the idea.

My brain just needs a reward to look forward to.

Otherwise it acts like a whiny bitch that wants to scroll X for 45 minutes and then pretend it’s working.

And here’s what’s wild.

You can literally reprogram yourself like that.

That to your brain doing a task = reward.

You are literally hacking your own brain chemistry.

Crazy.

And after a few weeks of this you start doing the work without even needing the reward anymore.

It becomes second nature.

So if you suck at starting, trick yourself.

Do a task, get a cookie.

Not literally.

Unless you want a cookie.

Then get a cookie.

Use anything that works for you.

But use it as a reward for your brain.

If you run a business and still don't have a website,

I am going to assume you hate money.

Sorry.

But a website is literally the most scalable sales person you can hire.

It doesn't need to sleep, doesn't need rest, works during weekends, it doesn't even take a day off because it's sick.

To make that happen, you need to:

- Add testimonials that are REAL and not FAKE
- add a clear CTA
- make it load fast
- and focus on speed, clarity, and conversions

And also to learn something new every day, people judge anything in about 0.5sec.

That means your website (or non existent one) as well.

So make sure that when someone lands on your website, they know

- what you do
- how you do it
- for who you do it
- results they can expect
- how they can contact you

Now, if you still don't have one and need help creating one or updating yours to reflect the value of your offer,

you know who to talk to 😉

Do you feel lazy?

Good.

That is what tonight’s email is for.

Not to motivate you.

But to turn you into a fucking machine.

Tonight's email is about SOPs and why they are the most boring but most life changing thing you can do for your business.

posts.text:
I am so tired of people saying they will start next week.

What the fuck is so special about next week?

Does next week give you a new brain?

Do you magically become smarter?

Do you get sent a 10k check for sitting on your ass?

No.

So you know the answer.
Most people lose because they do not even show up for the fight.

The sad truth about reality:

Nobody cares how hard you work.

They only care about the results you have to show.

And it's kinda true but also sad.

Let's say you have been going to the gym for 2 years (and you actually did).

But then somebody sees you in person or something,

and you look like you went to the gym once.

Idk how that could happen but lets say it did (because you only trained your eyebrows or something haha),

then that person who sees you is going to assume that you didn't go to the gym but instead have insane eyebrow genetics.

And the same thing is in business.

If you have a business and you worked on it for 3 years but have never closed a single client,

then we have 2 problems.

First off, you don't have a business because if you would call it a business, every person on earth would have one,

but secondly, others will think you just started.

And if you tell them you did this for 3 years already but just havent gotten results,

they think you're stupid.

Because you kinda are then.

How can you work for 3 years on your business and haven't closed a single client?

Either you worked on it every day for 3 minutes max or you just did everything apart from talking to people (which is THE thing that gets you clients).

So moral of the story would be to work on the tasks that bring you money in.

And in the early stages that is TALKING TO PEOPLE aka OUTREACH.

GM

You are a coach or consultant with no website.

Cool.

So you rely fully on DMs and referrals.

Which means that every new client you get is a miracle.

You post content, get 3 likes, DM 15 people, and close maybe one of them on a lucky day.

But what happens when someone checks your profile?

And then there is no website link?

Or even worse, there is a Linktree with 3 buttons that go basically nowhere?

Yeah, they disappear very fast and don't want to work with you anymore.

This happens EVERY SINGLE DAY.

But now imagine this.

You have a killer website with killer design, killer copy, killer everything.

The person visiting it will immediately trust you because you look like you care about your business.

Just because your website is on point.

And also the second they land on it, they know
- who you helped
- see results
- binge your testimonials
- feel your authority immediately

So they fill out the form you have or book a call even while you sleep.

That is what a good website does.

The right one can literally be better than your best sales person.

And it works 24/7 while you do not (because it's always online).

So if you are a coach without a website,

or even WORSE,

you have a website, but it looks outdated or doesn't work on mobile,

then you are burning money IRT (in real time).

Your clients are clicking and dipping because you failed the trust test.

So fix your website, or keep relying on luck.

Your decision.

If you want to fix your website though and want to seem like you take your business seriously,

my DMs are always open 😉

Most people ruin easy tasks because they make them 5 times harder.

I used to be the same.

Tonight’s email is about how I wasted money, doubled my work, and still thought I was being smart.

It is also about why simple shit works best.

posts.text:
Can somebody answer me this question:

why do I always get motivated to dominate the world when I am doing boring business tasks I don't want to do?

I am literally sitting here, doing outreach, and I all of a sudden have the motivation to get to 10k/mo in 3 days by doing more outreach.

I think it's a blessing but still.

Weird AF.
Nobody owes you shit except the version of yourself you could be.

How To Survive The Days Where You Don't Want To Work

Some days feel like someone hit you in the face with a brick the moment you wake up.

Happened to me this morning.

You look at your laptop.

You think about the 100 tasks you still have to do.

And your brain just won't turn on.

The problem is not that you do not know what to do.

The problem is that you already made a deal with yourself that you will do it tomorrow.

That is why you need to punch that bitch voice in your head right now.

Because there literally is NO TOMORROW.

YOU COULD DIE TOMORROW.

And if you think like that, a lot of stuff becomes urgent.

I do not care if you have to stand up, get a coffee, blast music, or talk to God for a second.

Because the moment you do the thing once when you don't feel like it, you will do it again the next time you feel like shit.

And so one completed task when you feel like not working is worth 10 completed tasks on a normal day.

Because it shows you that your word means something even when you do not feel like it.

Your coffee tastes like shit for the same reason your website is not making sales.

You put too much crap in it.

Every extra thing you throw in thinking it will make it better is making it worse.

So your website doesn't need all these animations you thought it needed.

It also does not need that sick button animation you saw on a YouTube video.

It needs to load fast, needs to be simple, AND it needs to show your offer in a way even a toddler would understand.

Stop adding shit to it.

It's just making it worse.

Start stripping it down until the only thing left is what actually makes people buy.

Got drenched in a storm today and walked away with a business lesson (as usual).

Tonight’s email is about why the worst conditions in life and business might be the exact thing that saves you.

And may be the reason you are stuck right now.

I hate when people tell me they just want to chill at 4pm.

Bro.

We live in a time where you can send a DM and make $1k the same day.

You can build a website in one weekend and have a business running.

You can turn one skill into an income stream.

And you are telling me you want to sit on the couch and watch Netflix?

Fucking loser.

Your content doesn’t suck because of the algorithm.

It sucks because it sucks.

Do you know that feeling where your brain wants to escape from the work you're doing because its boring,

but there is nothing to distract you,

and so you go into your kitchen or something?

And then you open the fridge out of boredom to do anything but the work?

I have that feeling every single day bro.

And something that I realized is that when you have that feeling that you don't want to work anymore,

you need to push through those 5mins that feeling is there.

Do that 12 times and you just worked for 15 hours straight.

I saw this in a Hormozi video a while ago but of course I didn't implement it because I thought I didn't needed it.

Now though because I notice myself that I need to focus more,

I am now applying exactly the advice from the video for myself.

And btw, imagine you would do this, push through the moment of distraction, every single day for a week or 2.

Bro where would you be?

You would outcompete almost everyone bro.

Anyway, that was what I had to say, now back to work.

GM.

Most people have never heard about the 60-30-10 color principle in design.

It is one of the simplest ways to make design look professional and actually aesthetically pleasing.

The way it goes is you pick one main color for 60 percent of the design,

then a secondary color for 30%, and the last 10% is the accent color.

This will make your design look 10x better bro.

And btw, it works on websites, logos, rooms, and even clothes.

The human eye just loves patterns and proportion.

Its from our evolution.

Human psychology.

So next time you design something, use that rule.

Or if you want the author of this post (me) to show you what this color principle looks like in action for you,

shoot me (a DM) 🔫

You fill every sentence with uhmmm, uhhh, you know, and you look like you never had a real conversation your entire life.

and how to fix it.

posts.text:
I hate how you can be in the middle of work and your brain just decides to replay the most random shit.

Like I am trying to get client work done and suddenly I am thinking about that one time in 2017 when I tripped over a dog leash and the dog started laughing.

Where does that even come from???

Or I will be designing a page and my brain will just throw in a memory of a random YouTube comment I saw 6 years ago.

Thanks brain.

Really helping me here.

It is like my mind has a team of unpaid interns who spend all day digging up the dumbest stuff possible just to distract me.

I need to fire them ASAP.
If your fridge light does not work you are likely not gonna make it in entrepreneurship.

Why I Hate Waiting

I absolutely HATE waiting for shit.

When I order something online and it says the delivery is in 2 weeks, my brain instantly starts looking for faster alternatives.

I don't even care if it's half the price.

If I can have it tomorrow instead of 14 days, I will buy it tomorrow.

That is how it is in business too.

Most of the time you wait for the perfect idea, or the perfect of ANYTHING really,

and if you didn't do that and just started working, you would already have landed 3 clients or something.

Because speed literally beats EVERYTHING.

People always talk about how it's important to be patient and not be too quickly in decisions and all that.

But then please tell me the last time when being patient for 3 weeks and not doing anything has worked out positively for you?

Right, you can't.

So if you have an idea, do it TODAY.

Or if you need a website, build the bare minimum TODAY.

DO IT TODAY.

If you don't do it today, you won't do it ever.

Just start immediately and figure out the rest while you are working.

If you want a website that gets you sales instead of just occupying space on some random server somewhere in China, do THIS:

- Make it painfully obvious what you sell in the first 3 seconds (If someone needs to scroll to get it, you fucked up)

- Have ONE call to action (It needs to be consistent across the page)

- Your offer needs to be so clear that even a drunk person who is half asleep gets it without errors.

- Make sure your website loads fast (I don't how how often I closed a website just because it didn't load fast enough)

- Make sure your website looks good on mobile (If you don't have a good mobile design, you basically are shitting on 70% of traffic)

Some people treat boredom like a disease.

They run from it, blast music or scroll on their phone to avoid it.

You should do the opposite though.

Tonights email is about why boredom is your biggest productivity hack

and why sitting with it will make you unstoppable.

I don’t trust people who bite into ice cream.

What the fuck is wrong with your teeth.

It’s the same as people who drink hot coffee in one gulp.

Psychopath energy.
You can’t lose if you never quit.

Why I Don't Listen To Music Before 2PM

I used to start my day off with music.

I would listen to it and thought I was getting myself hyped up.

What it actually did though is that it just made be distracted more and more and more and so I couldn't concentrate at all.

I would start singing random lyrics in my head and then not feel like working anymore.

Music killed my focus.

And so what I do now is I just sit in silence until 2pm until most of my work is done.

Most days not listening to music until 2pm turns into not listening to music the entire day because I just don't feel like listening to music.

But when I actually DO put music on, it feels more like a reward rather than something that distracts me.

Good Morning.

I don't know if you knew this, but visitors base trust on design.

And so if you have a great brand, but the design of your website looks trash, they will assume your service isn't that good as well.

How you do one thing is how you do everything.

So your website should of course have a good offer and stuff,

but also good design,

It should look aesthetically pleasing.

Most people always say that design doesn't matter when the offer is good.

That is only half true though.

Because the subconscious brain exists.

And it judges REALLY fast to identify whether there's a threat or not.

Evolutionary.

So make sure that the subconscious brain is satisfied by making the design great.

Some websites look clean.

And some people look like they know what they are doing.

But then you go to their website and they hide their prices COMPLETELY.

Tonight’s email is about how hiding your prices is literally ruining your business (and how to fix it).

posts.text:
I have no idea who invented the idea that 8 hours of work is hard.

It is not.

What is hard is pretending to work for 8 hours while actually doing 3 hours of work and wasting the rest.

That shit is exhausting.

Work like a maniac for 3 hours.

Then go do whatever the fuck you want.

It will feel like cheating.

Or just work for 8 hours FOR REAL.

The perfect morning routine:

Coffee, Prayer, Work, Gym, Food.

Then go live a normal life (or repeat this until evening)

Why I Will Never Trust People Who Eat The Pizza Crust First.

Who hurt you?

What childhood trauma unlocked that behavior?

The crust is the handle.

It is the thing you hold onto while eating the real part.

You eat pizza from the cheesy end down to the crust like a fucking civilized individual.

Not reverse that shit.

And these people always act cool about it too.

Like they just discovered a life hack.

“Oh it’s less messy this way".

No its fucking not.

You start with the crust and now you are holding molten cheese with your bare hands.

You are a danger to yourself and society.

Also it ruins the pacing.

The crust is the cooldown.

It is the after credits scene.

You do not open a movie with the credits.

That is sociopath behavior.

Anyone who eats the crust first cannot be trusted in business.

Ever.

If you want your website to print money in 2025, focus on this:

- Headline that solves a problem INSTANTLY.

- Subheadline that makes the problem feel urgent. "Why Now?".

- Button that says exactly what happens next. "Book a free call" for example.

- Proof like testimonials, screenshots, results, etc.

- Offer so clear that a drunk guy at 2am understands it.

- Layout that is easy to read. Space it out well.

- Every word should sell to the visitor.

Showing prices can make or break a sale.

Show too little and people think you are hiding something.

Show too much and they say no before they even know the value.

Tonight’s email is about how oversharing your pricing will kill your conversions.

posts.text:
You know what's weird?

When people say "Yeah I will start working on my business once school is over" or "once summer is over" or "once I get my new laptop".

WHAT DO YOU EVEN MEAN?

You can literally run a 5-figure business from a fucking iPhone 7.

What are you waiting for?

Apple to bless you with a device that types out cold DMs for you and closes the client too?

Shut up and get to work.

The internet is not gonna last forever.

One day governments will regulate it with AI to the point where you need a license to send a fucking email.

So now is the time.

If you have a phone and braincells you already have everything you need.
You can outwork talent but you cannot out-rest laziness.

Why I Work When I Don’t Feel Like It

This morning I woke up and felt like shit.

I just mentally felt like absolute shit.

Every cell in my body wanted me to do nothing today.

So I made the only logical choice.

I made coffee, sat down, and opened my laptop.

And instead of giving in to my bitch voice, I decided to see what happens if I work for 10 minutes.

Ten minutes later, I was in the zone.

Funny how that works.

We all think we need to be motivated to get things done.

But we actually don't.

We just need to start.

Because starting is the hardest part.

Most people wait for a lightning bolt of motivation before they take action.

That’s why they are broke.

And here’s the fucked up thing.

The “later” voice always sounds sweeter.

It promises fun and confort and rest, but it robs your future.

The “now” voice might feel like it’s dragging you through mud.

But at the end of the day, it’s the one that gets you the life you actually want.

So the next time you feel like doing nothing, do something for 10 minutes.

You might just trick yourself into winning the day.

And if you don’t, you will know that you at least tried.

GM.

If your website is not making you money, here is probably why.

You built it for yourself, not the person who is supposed to buy from you.

You picked colors you like, words you like, and photos you like,

but none of it actually talks to your customer.

Here's how to fix it.

Write like you are talking to one real person.

Tell them what problem you solve.

Show proof you can solve it.

Then make it stupid easy for them to buy or book.

Everything else is useless stuff that just reduces your loading time.

Pretty and useless is still useless btw.

Simple and profitable is perfect.

So make it that.

There is a way to make people forget the price completely.

A lion wakes up and stretches.

A bird wakes up and sings.

We wake up and scroll to see if strangers liked our pictures.

That is sick behavior if you really think about it.

If you are not embarrassed by your first client project,

you started too late.

Why I Love Driving Without A Destination

I love driving.

Not to get somewhere but just for the sake of driving.

I could be driving in circles for 2 hours and it would still make me feel like I’m doing something right.

Some people need clubbing to feel alive.

I just need a decent car and a road that’s not ass.

When I was a kid I thought adults were weird for liking driving funnily enough.

Now I get it.

There’s something about that hum of the engine and being in control of something powerful that just clears your head.

Sometimes I imagine I’m living in a video game when I drive and doing shit like Squeeze Benz.

Driving is like therapy without having to talk to someone with a psychology degree pretending that depression is normal.

I am telling you this because it is one of the most peaceful things I can do to reset my brain.

Every time my mind gets cloudy or I feel like throwing my laptop out of the window after a shitty sales call,

I just go out and drive.

Either for 10 minutes or 2 hours.

And then I come back with 3 new business ideas and a need to sell harder than before.

No matter what happens in life,

if I still have a car and a road,

I’ll be fine.

B2B websites and B2C websites are not the same thing.

But for some reason 90% of people think they are.

That is why your conversions are in the gutter and your leads ghost you 100% of the time.

Let me explain it real quick before you waste more time working with the wrong designers.

B2C = Business to Consumer.

They are normal people who scroll fast, buy fast, and is usually very low ticket.

Ecom stores sell to those.

They are impulse driven.

You need to sell the dream.

If you run a B2C brand, look at websites like Zalando or something and you have a competitor.

Now B2B.

B2B = Business to Business.

They make slow decisions, there's more money involved, and they want to compare options.

You need logic to get them to buy.

And of course proof.

You talk to people who are afraid as hell to make the wrong choice once again.

So if your B2B website looks like a trendy fashion store with minimalist design, then you need to rework that shit immediately and pay me to do that for you.

It is insane how many founders use the same structure for both.

Same sections, headlines, and also the same testimonials.

They use just slightly different colors and fonts.

That's not good enough.

If you sell to people,

build for emotion.

If you sell to companies,

build for decision makers.

Infinity makes my head hurt.

Every possible version of you exists RIGHT NOW.

Some versions are crushing it while you are stuck scrolling X.

Tonights email is about why that thought pisses me off and also lights a fire under me.

3 deadly sins I see on 99% of local business websites.

Sin #1:

You never know what the business is actually doing in the first 3 seconds because they have a hero section of some skyline and text over it saying some dumb shit.

Most simple mistake to make.

So change it to 3 things:

- What you do
- Who you help
- What to do next

That's it.

Sin #2:

Most local business websites try to be cool.

However that is a quite bad idea because they aren't a tech startup.

They are some local plumbing business in Stuttgart, Germany (my favorite football team ever btw).

I was on a barber page a few days ago and there was one CTA on the entire page.

You need minimum 3 Call To Actions per page.

One at the top, one somewhere in the middle,

and then one at the bottom.

posts.text:
I do not understand people who go to bed and just leave tasks unfinished.

How the fuck do you do that?

How do you lie there peacefully knowing you could have sent that one message or finished that one task and just chose not to?

My brain would explode.

My chest would feel like it's being punched from the inside.

Sleep is important, I know.

But so is not being a lazy piece of shit.

If you have something left to do and you’re thinking of leaving it for tomorrow,

don’t.

Do it now.

There is no tomorrow.
Your success is hiding under your to-do list.

The Inversion Principle

Charlie Munger said something that stuck with me forever.

Instead of asking "How do I succeed?" you ask "How do I fail?" and then avoid those things.

It is stupidly simple but extremely true.

Think about it in terms of business.

You do not ask "How do I get rich?".

You ask "How do I stay poor?".

And the answers to that are:

- Procrastination
- Ignoring opportunities
- Never learning new skills
- Spending money like a dumbass
- Hanging out with losers

Now you just need to avoid all of that.

Same with health.

You do not ask "How do I get fit?".

You ask "How do I get fat?".

- Eat junk
- Never move
- Sleep like shit
- Drink every weekend

Then just avoid that and boom, you are fit.

This principle works everywhere.

Money.

Relationships.

Fitness.

If you do not know what to do, just ask yourself what would make everything worse and then refuse to do it.

That way you cut off half the mistakes before they even start.

Here is why your website sucks and is not making money.

1. It loads like a grandma walking uphill with a broken leg.

2. It is confusing as f*ck.

3. You talk about yourself too much.
Nobody cares about your mission.

4. No trust signals.
No reviews, no guarantees, no proof.
If I do not know you, why would I give you money?

5. It is ugly.
I am sorry.
But design matters

Fix those 5 things and you will actually see people buy.

Ever thought about asking what would guarantee you to fail and then just avoiding that?

It sounds dumb but it is actually the smartest thing you can do.

Tonight’s email is about that exact inversion trick.

It can be used in client acquisition, fitness, and more.

Your $0 income does not need a fucking morning routine.

Wake up and get to war.

Your crystals can wait.

It’s pouring rain outside right now.

People are out there walking with their umbrellas getting hit sideways by the wind and rain.

And I am in here.

Standing in a fucking T-shirt.

Completely fine.

Do you understand how insane that is?

Water is literally flying from the fucking sky at lightning speed,

and I'm in here just vibing.

Houses are so underrated it’s actually insane.

These four walls are protecting me from a full-on natural disaster right now.

I’m watching people suffer.

From my little comfy cave.

With heating and lights and internet and steak in the fridge.

And no one talks about this shit.

Nobody is ever grateful for buildings.

We’re just complaining about the most useless shit of life.

Bitch your life is incredible.

You have shelter.

You are inside.

You are not getting slapped in the face by sideways rain like 90% of the people I just saw.

Houses are peak engineering.

I have no clue who the first guy was that stacked rocks on top of each other until rain stopped hitting him.

But that dude deserves a national holiday.

Anyway.

Just felt like talking about this.

Because I’m dry.

And they’re not.

Sales is literally the best skill on Earth.

Not because of the money.

Because you learn how to make people feel something.

You sell the feeling and not the product.

Nobody buys a website.

They buy the version of themselves who looks more professional.

Nobody buys your copy.

They buy how it makes their customer feel when they read it.

It’s always emotion first.

Logic later.

You can sell dog shit if you can make it FEEL like gold.

You can have the best product in the world and still starve if you do not know how to make someone feel desire.

This is why most websites flop.

They just look “nice” and explain too much and therefore do not sell.

A good website makes someone think that they NEED to work with you.

Same with copywriting.

Good copy is not poetic bullshit with big words.

It is raw emotion.

It cuts straight into your customer’s brain and says “you need this or you will keep suffering”.

That is sales.

And it is what I build when I build a website.

If it does not make someone feel, it is trash.

And trash does not sell.

I worked for 5 hours straight.

In a pitch black room.

And got more shit done than I usually do in 2 days.

Tonight's email is about the most fucked up focus hack I have ever tried.

I still cannot believe it works this good.

From 3 or 4 p.m. until evening I become borderline useless.

I can’t concentrate on anything.

Nothing works.

But the morning I’m zoned in with caffeine.

Absolutely laser focused.

From waking up till around 2 p.m. I am working with 120% concentration.

Every client message gets handled.

Every task gets smashed.

But then 3 p.m. hits.

And boom.

My brain starts falling apart in real time.

The productivity dies off faster than an electric vehicle discharges bro.

And no matter what I do, I can’t get anything good out of my brain anymore.

Absolutely insane.

Might need to start working 6 a.m. to 2 p.m. like a fucking freak and just accept that anything after that is extra credit.

Your brain is a machine.

Use it while it still runs.

Best thing ever:

When you talk to someone just to talk to them,

not to sell but just to connect,

like you are old friends who randomly bumped into each other in the street and now you're just standing there talking for 2 hours like you have nowhere to be.

And then the conversation starts to get weird because you run out of things to say.

Instead of forcing some weird business question down their throat.

You just say the truth.

"Feels like we ran out of stuff to talk about haha".

That alone builds more trust than any outreach script ever could.

Because you are not acting like a salesman.

You are literally just a human.

And then, because you said that and your mind starts moving,

you just randomly say what you are thinking about right now.

"Was just thinking about how fucked up it is that airports charge 9€ for a bottle of water"

Or

"I just realized that most of my best convos start with awkward silence".

Whatever thought you have in that moment.

You say it.

And then you ask them.

"What do you think?".

It sounds too simple to be true.

But I swear.

This right here is how I built 90% of the strongest connections in my network.

Talk like a friend.

Be honest when the convo goes quiet.

Say what’s on your mind.

Ask what they think.

If you do that,

people will remember you.

Because you treated them like a human instead of a walking wallet.

If your website looks like it was built during the Cold War,

you are done.

That is why I hate slow replies from clients.

You are losing out while you are out here deciding what fucking font to pick.

You do not need a perfect website.

You need one that just converts.

Most of you treat your website like a painting instead of a machine.

And the slower we build the machine,

the longer you stay broke.

I do not build pretty websites.

I build sales engines.

Sometimes I hate the design part.

It is boring as fuck.

But I like the money part.

And I like making your phone ring.

If that is what you want, cool.

If you want to “revamp your vibe” then I am not your guy.

I have a VERY weird fantasy.

It kicks in every time I hit the highway.

It involves speed, risk, and ZERO clothes.

Tonight’s email is about my fantasy that gets triggered by the left lane in Germany.

Worse than adult fantasies...

posts.text:
Why You Regret Buying Shit Only When You Don’t Have Money For The Next Thing

I realized something about regret.

It never shows up when you buy something.

It shows up later when you want something else but your wallet is empty.

That is when you start hating yourself for buying that hoodie or those headphones or whatever.

But when you are rich you never regret it.

Because you can just buy the next thing too.

That means the real solution to regret is not buy smarter or save more cash but to make so much money that regret doesn't even exist in your life anymore.

If you want to actually get clients online, stop hiding behind your laptop.

The formula is simple.

Have a profile that looks like you know what the fuck you are doing.

Send a lot of messages to people who fit what you offer.

Make the offer clear enough so they do not have to think about what you mean.

Do this every day.

Most people send 10 messages in one week and then cry about not getting clients.

No wonder you’re not getting any clients with 10 DMs a week.

There are people sending 100 DMs a day.

It’s all about VOLUME.

I do not understand how people NEED music.

Some people cannot go a single walk without blasting something into their ears.

Are your thoughts really that bad?

I can literally walk in silence for an hour and it feels normal.

Some people act like silence is torture.

Unreal.

Just do what you know you need to do regardless of how you feel and then your place won’t be as bad of a place to be in as it is right now.

Coffee solves 90 percent of my problems.

The other 10 percent just need more coffee.

Why Gratitude For The Tiniest Things Changes Everything

People think gratitude is just for Christmas gifts and birthdays.

But it is way deeper.

I started being grateful for small shit.

Like a green traffic light or the fact that my water is clean.

And suddenly life feels way happier.

Because you are stacking wins every single hour.

When you practice that, nothing feels ordinary anymore.

It all feels like a blessing.

And that keeps you hungry for more.

Most websites look like they were built for designers to jerk off to instead of making money.

THey have pretty pictures and fancy animations and all that bullshit.

But here is what actually makes money.

When someone lands on your website they should instantly know 3 things.

What you do.

Who it is for.

How to buy.

Every extra second they need to figure out these three things is a second where their subconscious is thinking about leaving.

So before you even think about colors, ask yourself:

Can a drunk person at 2am understand what the fuck I do in 5 seconds?

And if not, you now have another task on your checklist.

Or just message me and I can fix that for you.

Doubt feels like shit.

But it might be the EXACT thing that saves your business.

Tonight’s email is about why doubting yourself is actually a good thing.

And also the different kinds of doubt there are and which of those are fixable and not.

BE GRATEFUL TO BE BORED BRO.

Procrastination makes zero sense when you actually think about it.

You have a task to do.  

Let’s say it takes 1 hour.  

Now if you do it right away, that’s 1 hour of pain and then freedom.  

But now lets say you procrastinate.

You don’t escape the pain doing that.  

You just stretch it.  

Instead of 1 hour of discomfort, you give yourself 5 hours of dread before you even start.  

So the task still takes 1 hour.  

But now it feels like it cost you 6.  

And during those 5 hours of avoiding, you can’t even enjoy anything really.  

Because in the back of your head, you know the task is still waiting.  

So procrastination doesn’t save you anything.  

It doesn’t give you relief.  

It just multiplies the pain and drags it out.  

That’s why the people who just do shit fast look like they have more time.  

Because they aren’t living under a cloud of half-done things all day.  

Procrastination is basically paying interest on pain.  

Do it now, and it’s over.  

But if you do it later, and it grows into something way bigger than it ever needed to be.
Discipline feels like hell today but heaven tomorrow.

Sleep Is Insane

Last night I must have had a cramp in my left foot while I was asleep.

I only noticed it this morning when I woke up and felt the aftermath of it.

But the thing is that while I was asleep,

my brain didn’t just let me feel the cramp.

It went and made up this random ass dream where I was sitting at a bus stop.

And at that bus stop, I suddenly got a cramp which didn't go away at first.

Only after what felt like 20mins.

Like bro what the fuack??

My body is in real pain, but my brain creates a dream out of it for fun or what?

It’s insane.

And the craziest part is that I woke up and could still feel the leftover pain in my foot from that cramp.

The brain is so complex bro.

Imagine the house would be burning and I would be on fire and my brain just dreams that I am burning while I am actually burning.

Wtf?

I just saw a website with a popup that said "Subscribe to our newsletter for exclusive tips!"

WHAT TIPS BRO?

Tips about how to make honey in 3 minutes or how to kill pigeons?

If the tips would be about how to kill pigeons I would gladly subscribe.

But why would I want tips from someone who can't even tell me what his tips will be about?

This is like walking up to a stranger and asking for their phone number without even introducing yourself first.

It just seems weird and desperate.

If you want my email address, you need to tell me exactly what I get in exchange for giving you it.

Be specific in everything.

The fastest way to increase your website conversion rate (backed by science):

Remove everything that doesn't directly lead to a sale.

So if you have an about section about which coffee you like that doesn't lead directly to the sale.

So remove that.

Or if you have a blog with 200 posts but one like per post, you can delete that shit too.

You need to only focus on one thing:

- One specific problem that you solve
- One specific person you help
- One specific outcome you deliver
- And one way to contact you

Everything else is stuff that nobody cares about.

Just used Claude for the first time ever in my life.

And now I am thinking how I was able to use ChatGPT for over 2 years and never be bothered to try out Claude.

Bro it's soooo much better for just anything.

ChatGPT invents random shit when trying to do coding, or for example writing tasks are SO FUCKING BAD when ChatGPT does them.

However I just told Claude to write copy for a landing page I'm working on and BROTHER.

It's better than anything ChatGPT ever gave me in its entire existence.

And thing is I didn't even use a different prompt.

I think I'm gonna move to Claude instead of ChatGPT soon honestly.

Haven't figured out yet though if they have somethinglike custom GPTs too.

Because that's a huge benefit of ChatGPT.

Every successful website follows this exact structure:

Header: Who you help + what you do

Section 1: The problem they have right now

Section 2: What their life looks like when that problem is solved

Section 3: Why you are the person to solve it

Section 4: Exactly what they get when they work with you

Section 5: How much it costs

Section 6: How to get started

Six sections.

Everything else is stuff that doesn't need to be there and just kills conversions.

You need to just stop reinventing the wheel and just copy what works.

I love driving on empty highways at night with no music at all.

There is no traffic and also nobody who drives 80kmh when there are 120 allowed.

If you can't drive fast then just walk bro.

You would be faster walking than driving.

Anyway.

There is something about having complete control over where you go and how fast you get there.

The real freedom is literally building a business, making your own schedule,

and then driving wherever the fuck you want how fast you want.

THE MOST UNDERRATED WEBSITE HACK:

Your website should feel like a conversation with your best friend.

And so here is how to make that work:

Write how you actually talk.

If you wouldn't ever say the word "utilize" in your everyday life, don't put it on your website.

Say "use" instead.

Or if you would not say "We are delighted to assist you with your business transformation journey", do not put that garbage anywhere near your website.

Say "I will help you fix your business" instead.

Just sound like a human being.

Best conversion hack there is.

When I was on summer vacation, there were birds that would come to me every single morning.

And also regardless of whether it rained or stuff.

People need to be more like birds.

Because no matter if the weather is shit or whatever, the bird still gets up and does something.

Most people though skip their workouts because they don't feel like it or are scared what other people might think about them.

You would achieve so much more in your life if you would just be like the birds and do stuff whether you feel like it or not.

The biggest lie ever is to have your website work on all devices.

That's complete bullshit.

Your website needs to work on desktop and a modern phone.

It doesn't need to work on a fucking Blackberry something something.

But also probably 90% of website traffic is from phones.

But yet everybody tries to make the website look the best on desktop first.

Which is completely wrong.

You wanna make it look perfect on mobile and then only worry about desktop.

Because if your website sucks on mobile, your business will suck in general.

I can guarantee that.

The fastest way to lose a website visitor:

Make them think.

Every second someone spends trying to figure out what you do or how to contact you is a second where you messed up big time.

Your headline should be so clear that a 12 year old understands it.

Gotta be specifc.

A few examples:

If you say: "I help people" = What people? Help them do what?

Or "I provide solutions" = What solutions? For what problems?

Or even "I offer services" = What services? To who?

You need to answer these questions.

For example something you can say is:

"I help restaurant owners get 50+ new customers per month through Google ads".

Now that's some real shit.

So be more specific.

Your website homepage should be clear.

But how do you test that?

By doing a little game.

Show some friend or something your homepage for 5 seconds.

And after 5 seconds take it away again.

Then ask them:

- What do you do?
- Who do you help?
- How much does it cost?

If they cannot answer all three questions of those then I'm sorry to inform you but your page absolutely sucks then.

And most websites fail that test completely btw.

So if yours doesn't, you're on a very good path.

(btw I make them not fail that 😉)

They had:
- Phone number
- email
- contact form
- WhatsApp
- Telegram
- Instagram DM
- Facebook messenger
- and finally LinkedIn

Who even has so many contact things in the first place?

But anyway it's not helpful to have so many fucking options.

They should just have 1 single option.

And that should be the contact form in most cases.

So make it EASY for people to contact you.

Because otherwise they just will not contact you no matter how many options you give them.

Amateur: "Welcome to our website! We are so excited you are here!"

Professional: "Get 20 new clients in 60 days without cold calling"

Tonight's email is about why free work usually fails and how to actually use it the right way.

I was on a website just now that had a popup that popped up (what a wonder) and it asked for my email address before I even could finish reading the first sentence.

What kind of psychopath behavior is this?

Imagine walking into a store and having someone immediately ask for your physical address before you even look around.

You would leave instantly.

Rightly so.

And the same shit happens online.

You need to let people read your content first.

Give them some kind of value first before asking for something.

Simple reciprocity.

Earn the right to ask for their email first.

WIIFM?

Whats In It For Me?

That's the question that your website should answer BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE.

Every sentence on your website should pass that test.

A few examples:

"We have been in business for 15 years"

Cool! What is in it for me?

"Our team is passionate about helping people"

Cool info. What is in it for me?

"We offer comprehensive solutions"

I'm impressed. What is in it for me?

Nobody cares about YOU.

Not even most of your friends.

So why should a random visitor care about you?

The visitor only wants to know what specific benefit they can get from working with you.

That's the ONLY THING.

There is a cat in my neighborhood that every morning comes sprinting at me.

It's such a little thing but almost every morning when I leave the house this cat comes sprinting at me and wants to get petted.

Sometimes I'm really in a hurry, but I just can't ignore the cat.

It's impossible.

I literally HAVE to pet the cat for 1-2mins when coming to me.

No matter how little time I have I just can't ignore it.

Crazy what animals can do.

The 2 most expensive words you can possibly put on your website:

"Starting at..."

This tells the visitor that you have no confidence in your pricing whatsoever.

Also gives them the impressions that your prices are negotiable.

Say a fixed price or a pricing range with the higher price visible.

That makes you seem way more confident.

The best converting headlines are boring AF.

"Get 50 new clients in 90 days"

"Transform your business with our revolutionary client acquisition methodology that has never been seen before"

Which one do you think will print?

EXAAACTLY.

Numero uno.

Reason being that it is clear.

And the less clear it is, the less clarity the visitor has whether to stay on your website or not.

I was at a gas station this morning and there was this dude in front of me who spent 5 minutes on which energy drink to buy.

FIVE FUCKING MINUTES.

For a 3€ purchase.

I am so glad I don't drink energy drinks.

But these are the same people that will spend 30 seconds on your website before deciding whether to hire you for 5k or not.

That's the reason that your website needs to hook people immediately.

Headline needs to be crystal clear so that the other person knows what you do in 2sec.

Value proposition needs to be known in 5sec.

And the action they should take should be obvious in 10sec.

If you can't do that, you will not make it far.

You literally have less time to convince someone to buy your high-ticket service than Red Bull has to sell their drinks.

Your testimonials are worthless.

Sorry to break it to you.

"Working with XYZ was amazing! He really helped our business grow!"

Cool.

That tells me exactly...

NOTHING.

You gotta tell me HOW he helped, what kind of growth there was, HOW MUCH growth there was, and also in what timeframe.

Good testimonials are specific.

"Ben redesigned our website and we went from 1.8k/mo to 5.5k/mo in 45 days without doing anything differently. It was just the website itself that changed."

THAT is a testimonial.

The first isn't.

So stop asking clients about how they felt about working with you.

And instead ask them about the specific results you got them.

The easiest way to improve ANY website:

Delete half of the words.

Then delete half of what is left.

Because most people say the exact same thing in 30 different ways.

And also keep your sentences short.

Because short sentences read way better than long sentences that are stretched over multiple lines and basically say the same thing over and over and over again because then you lose the attention of the visitor very fast kinda like it is in this post right now.

You get the point.

Short sentences require less mental bandwidth to read than long ones.

Another hack is to write as if every word you write would cost you 10€.

You would be able to say exactly what you want with 75% less words than usually.

I got a client 300+ email signups in under a week by doing the opposite of what every other website does.

Most websites show their email popup instantly.

Like a desperate person asking for someones number before even getting to know them.

Fucking annoying.

So I waited 60 seconds.

Those 60 seconds were to check if the visitor was actually interested in what they were reading,

and not just accidentally clicking around.

And then when the popup got shown I didn't have some generic ass thing to get tips or something.

The popup said that they get 10% off of their first order.

It had a REAL value proposition.

So it added real value to their life to enter their email address.

And the result was 300+ signups in less than 7 days.

If I would have shown the popup instantly like everybody else I would probably have gotten them 3 signups MAX.

But this is what psychology and targeting can do.

You need to stop treating every visitor the exact same.

Because the person who stays on your website for 60 seconds is 1000x more valuable than the person who closes it after 3 seconds.

So you need to target the right people at the right time.

Not everybody deserves your valuable discount popup.

I woke up this morning and I checked my phone.

Someone was thanking me for a website I built for him.

He was super grateful and happy.

WHILE I WAS SLEEPING.

That is what good service does.

It makes people grateful for what you did when you are literally ASLEEP.

Most people deliver services that are just good enough so that the client won't be to unhappy.

But when you overdeliver in every aspect,

you FEEL the gratitude and happiness from the other person.

Best feeling there is.

Try it out if you have a minute.

Your main headline should make someone think that they ABSOLUTELY NEED your service.

Not think about it and then continue to scroll because they "maybe could benefit from it a little bit eventually in 10 years when they have elephantas as pets".

This ties into copywriting.

You need to make your headline and hero section in general grab ATTENTION FROM THEM.

Just saw a dog chasing a tennis ball in a park I was walking by.

Bro 2 things.

Number 1: He was the cutest dog ever.

Number 2: That dog didn't care about anything else on this world apart from the tennis ball in that moment.

He literally had pure focus.

Most entrepreneurs could learn from this dog.

Because most people start 78 new businesses daily and say yes to just literally everything in order to make money.

They cannot commit to just ONE THING long enough to make that ONE THING work.

So they need to be more like that exact dog.

- Focus on the ball
- Chase it until you catch it
- And ignore everything else

The three words that kill conversions:

"Learn more here"

Sorry to break it to you but NOBODY ON THIS PLANET wants to "LEARN MORE HERE".

They either want to buy or book a call or get started.

"Learn more" is what you put when the visitor has no idea what you do.

And if that is the case your hero section sucks donkey balls.

So replace learn more with an actual CTA that makes CASH.

RANT:

Something that I don't understand and never will understand is how people can drink coffee after 12pm.

I literally do not get that.

I only drink one coffee a day MAX and that has a few reasons.

Number 1 my coffee tolerance doesn't increase so I never need more than 1 coffee to feel the effect,

and number 2 is that I will never have problems with sleeping due to caffeine.

Whenever I see someone drink coffee after 11 or 12 I get 1% disgusted.

Because I could never do that.

Coffee is something for when waking up to get you going.

I don't see it as something to boost your concentration because it doesn't do that.

It just makes you feel less tired.

Which is good in the morning after waking up but I don't see how that would help ANYONE in the evening.

RANT OVER.

Your website should have ONE primary goal.

Not 3 or 5.

ONE.

Every single page should push visitors toward that ONE SINGLE GOAL.

If that is to book a discovery call, every page should end with "Book a call".

Or if it is to sell a product, the CTA on every page should be "Buy now".

Because when you have multiple goals the visitor gets confused.

And as we all know...

Confused visitors don't take the action we want them to take.

The best websites are simple.

- One headline
- One button
- One offer

You don't need

- Popup notifications
- Video backgrounds
- Social media feeds
- Fancy animations
- Live chat widgets
- Parallax scrolling

You need clarity.

And if you don't have that, nothing will work in your life EVER.

Because simple is what matters.

STOP PUTTING YOUR MISSION STATEMENT ON YOUR MAIN PAGE BRO.

PLEASE.

I JUST AUDITED 2 WEBSITES AND BOTH HAD THEIR MISSION ON THERE.

BRO NOOOOOBOOODYYY CARES ABOUT THAT.

LITERALLY NO ONE.

DO YOU THINK A RANDOM STRANGER CARES HOW MUCH CALORIES YOU CONSUMED ON TUESDAY 2 WEEKS AGO???

I DON'T THINK SO.

SO DON'T ADD YOUR MISSION STATEMENT ON YOUR MAIN PAGE ON YOUR WEBSITE.

MAN I'M PISSED RIGHT NOW OVER SUCH A LITTLE THING BUT BROOOO.

The biggest mistake people make with website copy:

Writing for everyone.

Because as you probably heard countless times by now, when you write for everyone, you specifically write for NOBODY.

Example:

"I help businesses grow" - Which businesses? Grow how?

OR

"I help burned-out real estate agents close 2 extra deals per month" - Specific.

Do you see the difference?

If you write something specific, it converts.

But if you write some generic shit, you will reach nobody because nobody feels like they are being spoken to.

So the best way to write good copy is to pick one single person you want to write to and then write to them.

- Screenshots
- Testimonials

You write like a unconfident little first grader.

Just say:

- What they get
- Why it matters
- How it is delivered (1:1 coaching, done-for-you, etc)

Ideally in 2 seconds or less.

—

Section 4: Process

This removes fear.

Tell them EXACTLY what happens after clicking.

- Step 1: Book a call
- Step 2: Delivery
- Step 3: Handoff

People buy when they know what happens next.

So they should not need to guess.

—

Section 5: Proof Wall

Now its time to absolutely drop the hammer.

- 2–4 testimonials
- Keep them short but also emotional
- Add one long one if it fulfills the purpose

Every quote must have a face.

Otherwise people don't believe it.

Minimum:

you don't need to make winning easy.

you need to make losing hard.

most people do the opposite.

they try to make winning easy while leaving all the ways to lose right in front of them.

then they wonder why they keep failing.

let me give you the simplest example:

nutrition.

you want to eat healthy.

so you buy chicken, rice, vegetables, all the good shit.

great.

winning is now easier because you have healthy food available.

but you also have oreos in the cabinet and ice cream in the freezer.

so yeah, you made winning easy.

but you also kept losing easy.

and guess what happens at 9pm when you're tired and dont care about anything anymore?

you eat the oreos.

because losing was still easy.

now imagine this:

you throw out all the junk food.

all of it.

oreos, chips, ice cream, everything.

now when you're hungry at 9pm, what are your options?

chicken and rice.

or starve.

see, you just made losing hard.

and when losing becomes hard, winning becomes automatic.

because you removed the path of least resistance that leads to failure.

this applies to everything.

you want to stop scrolling?

delete the app where you scroll.

don't just "limit your usage."

delete it.

make losing hard.

you want to wake up early?

put your phone across the room or even into a complete different room.

not on your nightstand where you can hit snooze.

make losing hard.

you want to work more?

remove every distraction from your workspace.

no second monitor with youtube.

make losing hard.

see the pattern?

people think success is about willpower.

but it's really not.

it's about optimizing your environment.

if losing is easy, you will lose.

no matter how motivated you are.

because when you're tired, stressed, or bored, you'll take the path of least resistance.

thats just how the brain works.

and if that path leads to failure, you will simply fail.

but if you remove that path entirely,

then suddenly winning is the only option left.

and that is the moment when it becomes automatic.

i don't keep junk food in my house.

not because i have insane discipline.

but because i know that if it's there, i'll eat it.

so i just don't buy it.

i made losing hard.

and because losing is hard, eating healthy is easy.

i don't have social media apps on my phone (apart from X).

not because i'm some monk mode person.

but because i know if i have them, i scroll.

so i deleted them.

i made losing hard.

and because losing is hard, staying focused is easy.

this is the secret nobody tells you.

stop trying to make winning easy.

start making losing impossible.

cut off every easy path to failure.

and then winning becomes the default.

because it's the only option you left yourself.

total visitors

bounce rate (people who leave immediately)
scroll depth (how far people scroll)

run these numbers for 30 days.

eye-tracking studies show people scan websites in an F-pattern.

1. they scan across the top (left to right)

reading your headline.

2. they scan down the left side

skimming subheadlines and the first few words of each section.

in that first 3-second scan.

and heres the problem with that

humans follow eye direction

its instinctive

when someone looks at something we automatically look there too

researchers have tested this

if you put a photo of a person looking at a product people look at the product

if you put a photo of a person looking at the camera people look at the person

and if your hero image has the coach staring directly at the camera theyre directing attention to THEMSELVES

not to the cta

so visitors land on your website

see your face

look at your face because youre looking at them

and then what

they dont know where to go next

because you didnt guide them

your eyes should be pointing toward the action you want them to take

if the cta is on the right your photo should be looking right

if the cta is below your photo should be angled down slightly

if you want them to read your headline first you should be looking at the headline

this isnt some weird manipulation tactic

its just how human attention works

we follow where people are looking

so if your hero image is staring directly at visitors youre wasting one of the most powerful psychological cues you have

because instead of guiding them toward booking a call

youre just making them stare at your face for 3 seconds

and then they scroll away confused about what to do next

where are your eyes pointing

if something is easy to read it feels more true

this is called the fluency effect

and its why short words convert better than long ones

because your brain processes them faster

and equates that speed with certainty

so when you read “fix your offer”

but when you read “optimize your value proposition architecture”

your brain has to work

it processes “optimize”

then “value proposition”

then “architecture”

each word takes time

each word requires effort

and that effort creates doubt

because if your brain has to work hard to understand something

this is why simple language wins

not because people are dumb

but because the brain trusts what it can process instantly

complicated words make people pause

so if you want people to believe what youre saying

say it in words they dont have to think about

and its updated everywhere

most coaching websites lose 80% of potential clients in the first 8 seconds.

here's the exact framework i use to fix that (and why your website probably isn't converting):

the average coach's homepage:
- generic hero headline ("transform your life")
- wall of text about credentials
- vague benefits ("unlock your potential")
- contact form buried somewhere

result? 2% conversion rate.

here's what actually works:

1. HEADLINE FORMULA

stop writing headlines for yourself. write them for the voice in your visitor's head.

bad: "life coaching for ambitious professionals"
good: "you're making $10k/month but working 60 hours? let's reduce that to 20"

the difference here is specificity and that creates recognition.

recognition creates trust.

2. ABOVE THE FOLD STRUCTURE

you have 8 seconds. here's what needs to be visible without scrolling:

- headline (their problem + outcome)
- sub-headline (how you solve it)
- one clear cta button
- social proof indicator ("helped 14 coaches scale past $50k/mo")

that's it.

everything else is distraction.

3. THE CREDIBILITY LADDER

people don't trust credentials anymore. they trust proof.

your homepage should answer these questions in order:
- do you understand my problem? (headline)
- have you solved it before? (results)
- can you solve it for me? (process)
- what happens if i say yes? (cta)

most coaches answer these backwards. they lead with credentials (who cares) instead of understanding (what matters).

4. CONVERSION PSYCHOLOGY TRICKS

a) button copy matters more than you think:
- "book a call" = 3% ctr
- "see if you qualify" = 11% ctr

reason for that is that qualification flips the power dynamic. now they need to prove themselves to you.

b) remove navigation on your landing pages:
every link is an exit. if your goal is bookings, remove everything that isn't the booking flow. trap them (nicely).

c) use exit-intent popups with loss framing:
- "don't let another month go by stuck at $10k"
- "most coaches wait 6 months before fixing this. you don't have to."

loss aversion is 2x stronger than gain motivation.

5. THE 3 SECOND SCROLL TEST

open your website. scroll for 3 seconds. stop.

did you see:
- a specific problem you solve?
- proof you've solved it?
- what to do next?

if not, your website needs to change that because a visitor would be confused.

6. OBJECTION HANDLING

your faq section should address the real objections, not softball questions.

don't write: "what's your coaching style?"
write: "what if i've tried coaching before and it didn't work?"

don't write: "how long are sessions?"
write: "how fast will i see results?"

handle the fear directly. that's what closes because most websites dont do that.

7. THE TRIPWIRE OFFER SECTION

if someone's not ready to book a $5k program, give them a micro-commitment:

- free audit
- $95 training
- 15-min qualifier call

getting them to say "yes" to something small makes them 10x more likely to say yes to the big thing later.

this is basic sales psychology but most websites completely ignore it.

8. MOBILE OPTIMIZATION (where most of you are bleeding money)

69% of your traffic is mobile. your website needs to load in under 2 seconds and have:

- tap-friendly buttons (min 44px height)
- readable text without zooming (16px minimum)
- cta visible without scrolling

if your mobile website sucks, you're losing 2 out of every 3 potential clients before they even read a word.

9. THE REINVESTMENT SECTION

after someone books a call, your confirmation page should:

- reinforce their decision ("you just did what 90% of coaches won't")
- tell them what to expect next
- give them homework ("before our call, write down your revenue goal")

this kills buyers remorse and increases show-up rates by 40%.

10. ANALYTICS

stop obsessing over traffic.

track:
- bounce rate on homepage (should be under 50%)
- time on page (should be 60+ seconds)
- cta click rate (should be 8-12%)
- form completion rate (should be 30%+)

if these numbers suck, more traffic wont help. youre just pouring water into a broken bucket.
